cards.f: Angle for a pie chart sector
cards.b: (frequency ÷ total) × 360°. Shortcut: 360 ÷ total gives degrees per item.

cards.f: Frequency from a pie chart angle

cards.b: Proportions, not actual numbers. You cannot compare frequencies between two pie charts unless the totals are known.
Areas are in proportion to totals, so r₂ = r₁ × √(n₂ ÷ n₁).

cards.f: Common mistake with comparative pie charts
cards.b: Using the ratio of totals instead of its square root for the radius.
Row totals and column totals must both add to the grand total in the bottom-right corner.
Bars side by side, used to compare groups category by category.
Each bar is split into parts. Good for comparing totals and proportions.
Leaves in order, one digit per leaf, and always a key, e.g. 3 | 7 = 37.
Two data sets share one stem. Left leaves read right-to-left, so the key must show both sides.
It keeps the raw data and makes the median, mode, range and quartiles easy to find.
Back-to-back bar charts of males and females by age group, usually as percentages.

cards.f: Pyramid with wide base, narrow top
cards.b: High birth rate, high death rate, short life expectancy. Typical of a less economically developed country.

cards.f: Pyramid with narrow base, wide top
cards.b: Low birth rate, long life expectancy, ageing population. Typical of a more economically developed country.
Vertical axis not starting at zero, uneven scales, 3D effects, different-sized pictogram symbols, missing labels or key.

The radii of comparative pie charts are in proportion to the square ___ of their totals.
A comparative pie chart for 50 items has radius 2 cm. A chart for 450 items has radius ___ cm.
A population pyramid with a wide base and a narrow top suggests a ___ birth rate.
Every stem-and-leaf diagram must include a ___ .

short.q: In a two-way table, 30 boys and 30 girls chose tea or coffee. 14 boys chose tea, 11 girls chose coffee, and 33 students chose tea in total. Find: boys who chose coffee, girls who chose tea, and total students who chose coffee. [3]
short.model: Boys coffee = 30 − 14 = 16. Girls tea = 33 − 14 = 19. Coffee total = 16 + 11 = 27 (check: 33 + 27 = 60).

short.q: 80 students chose a favourite subject. 14 chose Art. Calculate the angle for Art on a pie chart. [2]
A pie chart for 150 sales in 2020 has radius 4 cm. Calculate the radius of the comparative pie chart for 600 sales in 2021. [2]
Draw an ordered stem-and-leaf diagram with a key for 41, 35, 52, 38, 47, 35, 44. Find the median. [3]
A population pyramid has a narrow base and a wide top. Describe what this shows about the population. [2]
short.model: A small proportion of young people and a large proportion of older people: a low birth rate and long life expectancy (an ageing population).
points: low birth rate / few young people
long life expectancy / many older people
